growth_signal.value: Several drug programmes showed efficacy in animal models; a €150M partnership with Sanofi and work with Johnson & Johnson

raised.value: over $110M across six rounds, including a €60M Series A and a $7.4M France 2030 grant

entry.idea: Designs new drug molecules with physics simulation plus generative AI, so a candidate medicine can be found before anything is tested in a lab.
entry.lesson: Pair AI with hard science it cannot fake; the physics makes the model trustworthy exactly where data is scarce.
entry.name: AQEMIA

growth.reason: No revenue or programme-count numbers are published; the signals are a €150M pharma deal and repeated funding.

market.reason: Finding new medicines faster and cheaper applies to every disease and every drug company in the world.

tech.reason: A physics-plus-AI engine spun out of a top science school, with programmes already working in animals; years of work to copy.

sources.title: Aqemia pushes the boundaries of medical research (French Healthcare)

entry.twist: Instead of learning only from past chemistry data, it computes how molecules physically bind using statistical mechanics, so it works where no data exists yet.
entry.who_pays: Big pharma pays for multi-year research partnerships, such as a €150M deal with Sanofi, while the company keeps its own drug pipeline.
entry.why_now: Computing power and generative AI now make exact physics calculations fast enough to run across millions of candidate molecules.
